On the two branches of ξ=log G, S_+>S_−; at every z_+=z_− meeting the derivative-difference has fixed nonzero sign −sgn(z(z−k)), because x and W have fixed sign. A common endpoint at each end would require opposite near-endpoint signs, impossible without an interior forbidden crossing. This covers negative and nonrational solutions; no truncated numerical integration is used to exclude them. Linearization around both explicit curves gives Λ_+=kJ(w)>0 and Λ_-=-kJ(w+k)<0, and expanding the return map at 0 gives +πvs u²+O(u³). A scalar monotone return map has no true integer-multiple subharmonics.
